*Originally shared on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/iangow_posit-package-manager-activity-7427451728028991488-K67U) on 2026-02-11 (UTC).*

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
[Download the PDF](r-binary-packages-linux.pdf).
:::

If you use RStudio on Linux (e.g., using the WRDS RStudio Server platform) and your packages are still compiling from source, do yourself a favour and follow the instructions [here](https://p3m.dev/client/#/repos/cran/setup)

Type `cat /etc/os-release` at the command line and use that information to answer the "what Linux distribution are you using?" question, then proceed with the Repository URL provided.

(I know there are other solutions for this, but this one comes with easy instructions.)

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Setup update - 10 November 2026

Posit’s interface has changed since this post. Its current instructions are to choose the CRAN repository, use **Select Distribution** in the repository menu to select a compatible Linux distribution, and then open **Setup** to obtain the repository URL. In RStudio, paste that URL into **Tools → Global Options → Packages → Primary CRAN repository**. See [Posit’s distribution instructions](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/user/r-binary-packages.html) and [R configuration guide](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/user/configure-r.html).

For Linux binaries, use the URL generated for the appropriate distribution rather than a generic source-repository URL. Posit also documents [R user-agent configuration and runtime dependencies](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/serving-binaries.html#r-configuration-steps-linux), which may matter if packages still compile from source.
:::
